transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Everyone keeps saying I’m way too thin and sick, but I honestly don’t see what the big deal is about my weight right now. I really only came in because my coworkers and the urgent care doctor insisted on it after a little dizzy spell at work. I think they're all just making a mountain out of a molehill.
Could you tell me your current height and weight, and have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

I don't know my exact height and weight off the top of my head, but I know I've lost some weight recently. My pants are hanging off me and I've had to punch extra holes in my belt, but I actually kind of like seeing the numbers on the scale drop. I feel fine, so I don't really see why everyone is so worried about it.
If you are female, have you noticed your menstrual periods stopping or becoming irregular since you lost weight?
Actually, I'm a man, so I don't get menstrual periods. That question doesn't really apply to me.
Since you've lost weight, have you noticed any decrease in your sexual interest or drive?

To be honest, I haven't really thought about that or had it on my mind lately. I've just been so exhausted from my warehouse shifts and trying to manage everything else going on in my life. It's really the last thing on my radar right now.
Are you actively avoiding certain foods or restricting how much you eat to keep your weight down, and do you have a strong fear of gaining weight?

Most days I just have coffee, maybe a banana or half a sandwich during my shift, and some soup or salad at night because I don't want to feel heavy. If I even think about eating something like pizza or dessert, I get this tight, panicky feeling in my chest and worry I'll blow up and ruin all my progress overnight.
Besides restricting your food, do you ever make yourself throw up, use laxatives or diet pills, or exercise excessively to control your weight?
No, I've never done anything like that. I don't throw up, take pills, or use laxatives, and I definitely don't have the energy to do any extra working out right now.
Even if you don't know exactly, do you remember what weight the urgent care clinic recorded, and about how tall you are?
I honestly don't remember the exact weight number they wrote down at the urgent care clinic. I'm around average height, I guess, but I didn't really pay attention to the scale when they weighed me.
Could you tell me approximately how many pounds you have lost, and what your weight was before this weight loss started?

I honestly don't know the exact number of pounds I've lost or what my starting weight was, as I haven't really kept track of those specific numbers. All I can tell you is that my pants are much looser now and I've had to punch quite a few new holes in my belt just to keep them up.
Along with a decrease in sexual interest, have you noticed any physical changes like difficulty getting or maintaining an erection since your weight loss started?
I haven't really noticed or thought about that, to be honest. With how exhausted I've been from my warehouse shifts, it just hasn't been a focus for me lately.
Have you noticed yourself feeling unusually cold or needing to wear extra layers when others around you are comfortable?
No, I haven't really noticed feeling unusually cold or needing to wear extra layers. I feel pretty much the same as everyone else around me when it comes to the temperature.
When you look at yourself in the mirror, do you feel that you look fat or that certain parts of your body are too big, even though others tell you that you are too thin?

When I look in the mirror, I don't see someone too thin or sick—I just see myself as fit, though maybe a bit tired from work. I'm terrified of letting my weight creep back up because I don't want to become that sloppy, out-of-shape guy my ex-wife used to nag me about. Staying lean is really the only thing that makes me feel like I'm doing something right in my life lately.
Since your weight loss, have you noticed a decrease or complete absence of your usual morning erections?
I honestly haven't paid any attention to that, so I'm not really sure. I'm usually just so exhausted in the mornings that my only focus is dragging myself out of bed for my shift.
Before you started losing weight and feeling so exhausted, would you say you had a normal, active interest in sex?
I haven't really thought about that, to be honest. Especially after my divorce and moving out, my mind has been entirely on other things. It just wasn't really something I was focusing on back then.
